cookwareFormats.name: Standard Household Aluminum Foil (16 µm / Bare 8011 Alloy)
cookwareFormats.pittingSensitivity: Extreme (Pinhole perforations occur within 30–60 min under acidic-saline exposure)
cookwareFormats.description: Standard thin consumer foil. Its nanometer-thin native Al2O3 oxide film is rapidly dissolved by organic food acids below pH 4.5. High flexibility and thin gauge maximize microscopic surface roughness, resulting in massive surface area-to-volume contact with acidic food liquids.

cookwareFormats.name: Heavy-Duty Aluminum Foil (24 µm / Bare 8011 Alloy)
cookwareFormats.pittingSensitivity: High (Resists mechanical tearing, but exhibits identical chemical dissolution rates)
cookwareFormats.description: Thicker aluminum sheet provides greater structural integrity and tear resistance for grill packets, but possesses identical chemical composition and surface passivation. Soluble aluminum migration into acidic juices occurs at virtually the same rate as standard foil.

cookwareFormats.name: Bare Commercial Aluminum Cookware (Un-anodized 3003 Stockpot / Sheet Pan)
cookwareFormats.pittingSensitivity: Moderate to High (Develops deep pitting craters, gray discoloration, and metallic off-flavor in tomato sauces)
cookwareFormats.description: Common in restaurant kitchens and bakery sheet pans due to superior thermal conductivity (218 W/m·K). However, prolonged simmering of acidic tomato sauces or reduction of vinegar glazes strips the oxide skin, leaching hundreds of milligrams of aluminum and imparting an astringent metallic flavor.

cookwareFormats.name: Hard-Anodized Aluminum Cookware (Electrochemical Sealed Sapphire Al2O3 Layer)
cookwareFormats.materialClass: Hard-Coat Anodized Aluminum (MIL-A-8625 Type III, 35–50 µm Al2O3)
cookwareFormats.pittingSensitivity: Extremely Low (Ceramic sapphire coating resists acids down to pH 3.0 unless mechanically gouged)
cookwareFormats.description: Undergoes an electrolytic acid bath process that converts the surface into an ultra-dense, diamond-hard aluminum oxide ceramic layer 10,000x thicker than native foil passivation. Pores are hot-water sealed, preventing organic acid molecules from contacting elemental aluminum.

cookwareFormats.name: Dual-Layer Barrier: Parchment Paper Lined on Aluminum Foil
cookwareFormats.materialClass: Bleached/Unbleached Cellulose Parchment Barrier with Outer Aluminum Backing
cookwareFormats.pittingSensitivity: Zero Direct Metal Contact (Cellulose and silicone release barrier completely isolates food)
cookwareFormats.description: The gold-standard culinary safety technique: unbleached silicone-coated parchment paper directly contacts the acidic marinade, while external aluminum foil crimps over the outside to lock in steam, moisture, and oven heat. Yields zero detectable aluminum migration into food.

cookwareFormats.name: 304 / 316 Surgical Grade Stainless Steel Cookware (18/10 Cr-Ni)
cookwareFormats.materialClass: Austenitic Stainless Steel (UNS S30400 / S31600, 18% Cr, 10% Ni, 2% Mo)
cookwareFormats.pittingSensitivity: Negligible (Self-healing Cr2O3 passive film is completely immune to aluminum leaching)
cookwareFormats.description: Completely aluminum-free food contact alloy. Self-healing chromium oxide passivation provides robust resistance against organic acids, citric marinades, and high-salinity tomato purees without metallic ion breakdown.

cookwareFormats.name: Enameled Cast Iron / Ceramic Dutch Oven (Vitreous Borosilicate Glass Coating)
cookwareFormats.materialClass: Vitreous Enamel Fused to Heavy Cast Iron Core (Zero Aluminum)
cookwareFormats.pittingSensitivity: Zero (Inert non-porous glass glaze prevents all metal leaching)
cookwareFormats.description: Vitreous mineral glass glaze bonded to heavy cast iron. 100% non-reactive across all food pH levels (pH 1.0 to 14.0), making it the premier choice for 8-hour acidic tomato marinara simmering and vinegar braising.

acidicFoodMatrices.name: Lemon / Lime Juice & Herb Marinade (pH 2.2, Concentrated Citric Acid)
acidicFoodMatrices.bioavailabilityEnhancement: 9.5x (Citrate ligands form neutral, highly soluble Al-citrate complexes that cross human intestinal tight junctions easily)
acidicFoodMatrices.description: Extreme chemical reactivity. Citric acid is a tridentate tricarboxylic chelator that rapidly depassivates Al2O3, forming soluble [Al(Cit)] complexes. Citrate simultaneously acts as a human intestinal transport enhancer, increasing systemic aluminum bioavailability up to tenfold.

acidicFoodMatrices.name: Tomato Marinara Sauce / Paste / Ketchup (pH 3.8, Citric + Malic Acid & 1.8% NaCl)
acidicFoodMatrices.primaryAcid: Citric Acid (~5 g/L) + Malic Acid (~2 g/L) + Sodium Chloride (1.8% NaCl)
acidicFoodMatrices.bioavailabilityEnhancement: 5.2x (Synergy between chloride ion pitting corrosion and organic acid solubilization)
acidicFoodMatrices.description: A devastating combination for aluminum foil. Organic acids dissolve the surface oxide film while chloride ions (Cl-) infiltrate microscopic grain boundaries, triggering intense localized pitting corrosion. Foil wrapped over lasagna or baked chicken frequently develops open pinholes within 45 minutes.

acidicFoodMatrices.name: Balsamic / Apple Cider Vinegar Marinade (pH 2.8, 5% Acetic Acid)
acidicFoodMatrices.description: Strongly acidic marinade. Acetic acid dissolves the passive amphoteric oxide layer, generating soluble aluminum mono-, di-, and triacetate salts that diffuse freely through cooked meats and vegetables.

acidicFoodMatrices.name: Buttermilk / Greek Yogurt Tandoori Marinade (pH 4.1, Lactic Acid & Emulsified Fats)
acidicFoodMatrices.primaryAcid: Lactic Acid (Alpha-Hydroxy Acid, ~12 g/L) + Dairy Lipids
acidicFoodMatrices.bioavailabilityEnhancement: 3.8x (Emulsified milk fats suspend dissolved metal salts across food surface)
acidicFoodMatrices.description: Moderate acidity coupled with lipophilic emulsion. Lactic acid coordinates with aluminum ions, while dairy butterfat and spice oils act as carrier matrices that hold leached metal ions against the surface crust of poultry during baking.

acidicFoodMatrices.name: Brown Sugar & Molasses Barbecue Glaze (pH 3.6, Acetic + Citric + Reducing Sugars)
acidicFoodMatrices.primaryAcid: Acetic & Citric Acids + High Fructose Corn Syrup / Molasses Glaze
acidicFoodMatrices.bioavailabilityEnhancement: 4.5x (Caramelized sugars bake directly onto foil, stripping aluminum flakes upon peeling)
acidicFoodMatrices.description: High temperature causes reducing sugars to caramelize and bond firmly to the corroding aluminum foil. When foil is peeled off ribs or chicken, microscopic flakes of metallic aluminum and concentrated aluminum salts are mechanically stripped directly into the meat bark.

acidicFoodMatrices.name: Neutral Olive Oil, Garlic & Rosemary Roast (pH 6.2, Non-Acidic Baseline)
acidicFoodMatrices.primaryAcid: Minimal / Oleic Acid (Fatty acid with zero chelation capacity at neutral pH)
acidicFoodMatrices.description: Neutral cooking environment. The Al2O3 passivation film remains intact and thermodynamically stable between pH 5.5 and 8.0. Aluminum migration remains beneath 0.2 mg/kg, presenting negligible health risk.

cookingThermalProfiles.name: Cold Refrigerator Storage (4°C / 40°F, 24 Hours Contact)
cookingThermalProfiles.description: Sub-ambient kinetics. While cold temperature suppresses reaction velocity, extended 24-hour dwell time permits slow acid etching of foil wrapped tightly around half-cut lemons, tomato halves, or acidic leftovers.

cookingThermalProfiles.name: Countertop Marinating (22°C / 72°F, 4 Hours Contact)
cookingThermalProfiles.description: Standard room temperature marinating in foil-lined dish. Chemical dissolution proceeds steadily; chloride ions begin forming microscopic pitting cavities beneath lemon or vinegar pools.

cookingThermalProfiles.name: Low & Slow Braising / Smoker (120°C / 250°F, 180 Minutes)
cookingThermalProfiles.description: Extended thermal braise in tightly sealed foil pouch. Constant internal steam reflux bathes the ceiling of the foil packet with hot acidic vapor and condensed droplets, causing widespread diffuse etching.

cookingThermalProfiles.name: Standard Oven Roasting / Baking (180°C / 350°F, 60 Minutes)
cookingThermalProfiles.description: Classic roasting of foil-wrapped fish, chicken breasts, or vegetables with lemon slices. Marine juices boil at the foil interface, driving rapid electrochemical dissolution into the cooking liquid.

cookingThermalProfiles.name: High-Heat Grill / Broil in Foil Packet (220°C / 425°F, 45 Minutes)
cookingThermalProfiles.description: Direct radiative heat flux. Localized foil hotspotting accelerates chemical reaction rates exponentially (Arrhenius activation), driving aluminum ion migration to peak concentrations of 200–500 mg/kg food.

galvanicCoupling.name: Isolated: Placed in Pyrex Glass / Ceramic Baking Dish
galvanicCoupling.description: Zero dissimilar metal contact. Dissolution proceeds purely via chemical acid-base chelation and thermal diffusion.

galvanicCoupling.name: Direct Contact: Lined on Stainless Steel Baking Sheet (Galvanic Couple)
galvanicCoupling.description: Creates an active galvanic couple. Stainless steel (+0.1V) acts as the noble cathode while aluminum foil (-1.66V) becomes a sacrificial anode. With acidic, salty marinade serving as the electrolyte, electron transfer drives catastrophic localized pitting and perforation.

galvanicCoupling.name: Direct Contact: Set upon Bare Carbon Steel / Cast Iron Grill Grate
galvanicCoupling.description: Significant potential difference (-0.44V iron vs -1.66V aluminum). In the presence of hot salty marinade drippings, aluminum preferentially corrodes, weakening foil packet seams and depositing dark metal oxides.

consumerProfiles.name: Standard Adult (70 kg Body Weight)
consumerProfiles.description: Healthy adult renal system clears approximately 95% of absorbed systemic aluminum within 48–72 hours via urine, but cumulative bioaccumulation occurs in bone mineral matrices and deep brain cortical tissue.

consumerProfiles.name: Lighter Adult (55 kg Body Weight)
consumerProfiles.description: Reduced body mass lowers the European Food Safety Authority Tolerable Weekly Intake threshold to 55 mg/week, making single high-exposure meals disproportionately impactful.

consumerProfiles.name: Young Child / Pediatric (20 kg Body Weight)
consumerProfiles.renalClearanceStatus: Immature Renal Excretion & Developing Blood-Brain Barrier
consumerProfiles.description: Children possess higher intestinal permeability and an immature blood-brain barrier. Tolerable weekly intake is capped at just 20 mg/week. A single serving of foil-baked lemon salmon can exceed 150%–300% of an entire week's safe ceiling.

consumerProfiles.name: Renal Impairment / Chronic Kidney Disease (70 kg, High Vulnerability)
consumerProfiles.description: Because kidneys are the sole excretory route for aluminum, patients with renal insufficiency accumulate toxic burdens rapidly. Bioaccumulated aluminum induces dialysis encephalopathy, microcytic hypochromic anemia, and severe osteomalacia.
